content: Supporters of Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 110, or BIP-110, have revived a breakaway minority blockchain network following an early August split. The restarted chain pairs a new mining algorithm with a significantly reduced block limit of 300 kilobytes. This development comes after the network had previously gone quiet following the initial split from the main Bitcoin chain.

The End of Point-in-Time KYC
summary: Most KYC programmes are still built around a picture. At onboarding, the institution assembles a p
content: Traditional Know Your Customer programs largely rely on point-in-time verification, capturing a static picture of a customer only at the onboarding stage. Financial institutions traditionally assemble identity documents at this initial moment. However, evolving industry standards and practices suggest a shift away from this outdated model toward continuous monitoring, ensuring that customer risk profiles remain accurate and up-to-date throughout the entire lifecycle of the business relationship.
